description: What is actually on the page, and what says it can be trusted. Every technical gate above only decides whether this gets read.

gates.title: No Route Is Thin
gates.rule: Each route carries enough of its own copy to answer the query it targets. A service page runs 800 words, a post 1,500, a category 400 - a route far under its type's floor competes with pages that are not.
gates.fix: Write the missing content, merge the route into a fuller one, or answer n/a naming the route as a shell that renders its copy from data.

gates.title: No Filler Copy Ships
gates.rule: No lorem ipsum and no placeholder prose anywhere in the markup. Filler indexes exactly as well as real copy does, and it is what the page then ranks for.
gates.fix: Replace each block with the real copy, or remove the section.

gates.title: The Answer Comes First
gates.rule: A long route states its answer in the opening lines rather than building to it. Roughly half of AI citations are taken from the first third of a page, and a buried conclusion is not quoted.
gates.fix: Move the direct statement to the top of each section and let the detail follow it.

gates.title: Content Is Attributed
gates.rule: An author is named. Experience and authorship are what the quality guidelines are written around, and anonymous content has neither to show.
gates.fix: Add a byline with a real person and link it to a page that says who they are.

gates.title: Dates Are Visible
gates.rule: Editorial content renders when it was published and when it was last changed. A reader deciding whether a page is current has nothing else to go on, and neither does anything reading it.
gates.fix: Render the dates on the page and mirror them into datePublished and dateModified.

gates.title: Headings Match The Question
gates.rule: At least some headings are phrased the way a query is. A heading that matches the question is the string a generative answer quotes, and a site of noun-phrase headings matches none of them.
gates.fix: Rewrite the section headings people actually search as the question they would type.
